summary: Delilah presses Samson with the same demand day after day until he tells her what he had kept secret. The Peshitta uses the corresponding verb both for a crowd pressing in and for a request pressed on an unwilling hearer.

words.summary: The single Hebrew occurrence gives both the means of pressure, repeated words, and its effect on Samson.

senses.definition: Keep pressing a person with a demand until resistance wears down.

evidence.note: Delilah presses him with her words day after day until he is weary to death.
Samson then tells her all his heart.

parallels.note: The preceding verb specifies that Delilah pressed him with her words.

senses.definition: People crowd someone physically, leaving little room.

evidence.note: Peter points to the crowds surrounding and pressing Jesus.

senses.definition: A person or circumstance presses someone to do something. The pressure can take the form of an urgent invitation.

evidence.note: The travellers press Jesus to stay because evening has come.
The people Paul describes try to compel others to be circumcised.

senses.definition: An obligation or need presses for a particular course of action.

evidence.note: Paul considers it necessary to send Epaphroditus back to the believers.

senses.definition: Experience the weight of trouble or find oneself compelled by circumstances.

evidence.note: Paul recalls a burden in Asia that exceeded his strength.
Opposition compelled Paul to appeal to Caesar.

senses.definition: Pressure that someone undergoes, whether bodily anguish or suffering at the hands of others.

evidence.note: The woman in labour experiences anguish until her child is born.
God sees the affliction of his people in Egypt and hears their groaning.

senses.definition: An entrance with little space to pass through.

evidence.note: The narrow gate stands opposite the broad gate.
Helping the afflicted is one of the widow’s good works.

senses.definition: A person who inflicts distress on another.

evidence.note: The people who afflict the believers are themselves to receive affliction.

cognates.note: Mandaic. One text describes pressing a seal, another a narrow street.

evidence.locator: p. 21, ALṢ, peal and passive participle; CP 90:10 and Q 56:12
Aramaic אוּלְצָן, variant אוּלְצָנָא, A00681, citing Targum Job 5:11

note: The shared root heading includes unrelated items. Key a.du.af is the conjunction אִם, already in im. Eltekeh and Eltekon are places, Elkoshite identifies Nahum by origin, and אַלְקוּם is a cross-reference to אַל. None supplies a personal name formed from this verb. SEDRA root 117 contains lexemes 154–157. The proposed Akkadian comparison šūluṣu needs verification of both form and sense. No independent Arabic counterpart was established.
